title: Why college applicants sound like AI even when they’re not using it
source_used: The Boston Globe (opinion by Ben Urwand)
key_facts: Author Ben Urwand runs Real College Essays, a tutoring service for applicants.
Parents report children's own essays flagged as 80% AI-generated by detectors.
He argues essays have become interchangeable over about 20 years of competition and online advice.
AI is trained on the same sample essays, so it copies the formulas admissions officers already see.
He says no detector can tell AI from a student following the same formula.
He urges colleges to reward essays that show a student thinking in a particular way.
quote_evidence: "AI did not create this problem. It simply made it more visible."
why_it_matters_hint: Offers an explanation for false AI-detector flags on college essays.
notes: Opinion essay, not news reporting; author has a commercial interest in essay tutoring.
